data.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer
data.authors: Carracedo A; Pandolfi PP et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTORC1 inhibition activates the MAPK pathway via a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in cancer.
data.abstract_excerpt: Numerous studies have established a causal link between aberrant mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) activation and tumorigenesis, indicating that mTOR inhibition may have therapeutic potential. In this study, we show that rapamycin and its analogs activate the MAPK pathway in human cancer, in what represents a novel mTORC1-MAPK feedback loop. We found that tumor samples from patients with biopsy-accessible solid tumors of advanced disease treated with RAD001, a rapamycin derivative, showed an administration schedule-dependent increase in activation of the MAPK pathway.

extracted_findings.effect: mTORC1 inhibition activates the MAPK pathway through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop (a resistance mechanism)
